title: GIOCA's refusal ladder re-implements the engine's rule outside `gameEngine.ts`
problem: `readStagedPlay` already calls `checkSelection`, which returns `{ok:false, code}` (stagedPlay.ts:57-61). It then throws `code` away and asks `playButtonLabel` again. `playButtonLabel` is a second copy of `beatRefusal`'s ladder (royal, bomb, type, length, tooLow), working on a lossy `ComboShape`.
proposed: `PlayButtonLabel` becomes `"play" | SelectionRefusal`. Equivalent wherever the label is read: `selectionLeaves.tsx:117-140` reads `reason` only when `!staged.playable`.
effect: Deletes about 50 lines (`playButtonLabel` and `ComboShape`). `turnTimerUi.ts` goes back to what its header says it is.
notes: #1596 is closed, but 01-table and 02-components re-verified that stagedPlay still discards check.code and asks playButtonLabel (kept both functions plus a parity test), so it is not fixed.

title: Hand-row geometry is buried in `StraightHand`, computed in three parallel loops; the tested hit-test is a decoy
problem: All of this is pure arithmetic (card size per turn, crop, arc solve, tilt overhang, `topClearance`, `heldCeiling`, slot, home and shift per card, strips, rotated hit test). It is locked inside a 22-prop memo component, so only a renderer or Playwright can reach it. The same per-card values are derived three times: `restY` at 1330 equals `y0` at 1085 (`rowBase + crop + home.y - cardH/2`).
proposed: A JSX-free `components/handLayout.ts` with `layoutHandRow(input): HandRowLayout` (card size, crop, arc, clearance, slots and per-card places) and a worklet `cardUnder(layout, x, y, shown, reduceMotion)`; `StraightHand` renders from it and `handTurnScale` imports it instead of re-implementing it.
effect: `StraightHand` drops about 200 lines of arithmetic, and the three loops become one. `handTurnScale` imports the real function instead of copying it.

title: The exchange's presentation is smeared across five modules, with GameTable holding its state machine
problem: No module owns "the exchange as the table shows it". GameTable keeps the stage-report state (`reported`, `exchangeSeq`, the render-time seq bump at 503) and derives `stages`, `choiceReady`, `exchangeIsMine`, `choiceOpen`, chip text, pile note, seat lit and shift, and giveable. ExchangeLegs reports stages back up through two callbacks, and the hand reads stages again via `useHandArrival`.
proposed: Interface: export function exchangeNotes(i: { shown: ExchangeAnnounceData|null; stages: ExchangeStages; view: ExchangeView; giveable?: Card[]; viewerSeat: number; spectating: boolean; nameOf: (s:number)=>string; t: TFn })
effect: About 90 lines leave GameTable, and the exchange's derivations sit in one file. `exchangeNotes` is a node test table (two-Jokers, receive at rest, give at rest, fallback giveback, watcher).
notes: 01-table: ui-F3 has only line drift; the two sentences also differ in grammatical person and leg selection.

title: Table geometry is a 12-field bag mixed with game state, fanned out field by field, and the layout is encoded twice
problem: `SeatGeometry` mixes frame geometry (scale, window, table edges, surplus, bottomPad, handCardH) with game state (players, opponents, viewerSeat). `ThrownPlayInput`'s own doc (flightPhysics.ts:560-565) says the fields are spread because naming a per-render object inside an effect trips `exhaustive-deps`. The interface shape is a workaround for missing memoisation.
proposed: `usePileFlight({ ...state, layout, seating, ... })`: the dependency list goes from 25 to about 12. Optional second step (L, high risk): render the top, side and centre sections at `layout.boxes` (absolute) so flexbox and the model cannot disagree.
effect: About 60 lines of field-forwarding go across GameTable, pile, deal, dealSlots and ExchangeLegs. One anchors computation per render.

title: Opponent seats: two near-identical slot components rendered three times with 13 identical props
problem: The slots' 12-prop interface is as big as their bodies (shallow). GameTable repeats the same 11-13 prop expressions per seat (`onMove(seat)`, `seatCount(...)`, `deal.arrivalsFor(seat)`, `passed.includes(seat)`, `vacatedOf`, `disconnectedSeats[seat]`, `seatCountdown`, `focusMode`, `seatMark(seat)`). About 60 lines of JSX that must change in three places.
proposed: Primitives stay primitive, so the memo still holds.
effect: About 70 lines removed from seats.tsx and about 60 from GameTable. "Fixed the top seat, forgot the sides" becomes impossible.

title: Hand-written memo comparators, with a source-parsing test to keep them complete
problem: Both comparators are shallow equality except for `card` (compared by id) and two mount-only props. Adding a prop and forgetting a line is a silent stale-card bug. The guard is a regex over interface text that breaks if the interface is restyled (e.g.
proposed:
Interface: export function propsEqualExcept

(by: { [K in keyof P]?: ((a: P[K], b: P[K]) => boolean) | 'ignore' }) : (a: P, b: P) => boolean; // iterates the union of both objects' keys; Object.is for the rest
effect: About 55 comparator lines are deleted, and so is the source-parsing test, replaced by a 5-case unit test of `propsEqualExcept`. A new prop is compared by default, so the forgotten-line class is gone.

title: Turn presentation: two parallel 5-way ternaries and two `turnTimerActive` calls in GameTable's JSX
problem: This is pure presentation logic inline in render. A branch added to one ladder and not the other makes the screen-reader sentence diverge from the chip. The two timer questions differ only in three inputs.
proposed: A pure `turnPresentation(input)` in `components/turnTimerUi.ts` returning `{ chip: { key, params, spokenKey }, clock: { active, resetKey, seconds }, seat? }`, so the chip text and the spoken sentence share one decision.
effect: About 50 lines out of the JSX. A node test table replaces the native mounts that today pin the chip text (`matchTurnChip`, `dealTurn`).

title: OS orientation lock lives in the table component
problem: A true-external dependency (UIKit/Android orientation plus a custom native module) is driven from inside the presentational table. The adapter's quirks (#1211, #1378) sit next to card logic. It is the only `ScreenOrientation` use in `components/`.
proposed: `export function useLandscapeLock(navigation?: NavigationLike): void` in `lib/device/orientation.tsx`.
effect: About 40 lines and 3 imports leave GameTable. `orientationFirstRender.test.tsx` and `orientationRows.test.tsx` can target the hook, and future orientation fixes do not touch GameTable.

title: "The play that ended the round has landed" is decided four times, behind a call-order contract
problem: Each hook re-derives "ended, nothing in flight, nothing pending" from `timeline.inFlight` and `timeline.pending()`. Each carries the same prose contract: it must be called after `usePileFlight`, because `pending()` is read at call time. That ordering is enforced by comment only.
proposed: `usePileFlight` (the module that owns the throw) returns `endedLanding(ended: boolean): number | null`, the landing time of the ending play or null. Alternatively, `tableTimeline` gains `landedSince(at: number): number | null`. The two hooks take that landing time as input instead of `timeline`, which also removes the ordering contract.
effect: Two copies of the gate and two ordering comments are deleted. A new ending consumer cannot read `pending()` before the throw is registered.

title: The lamp level has three writers that guess ownership from the target value
problem: Three effects write one `lvlT`. Two infer "this level is mine" by comparing the current target with their own constant, and the third does no inference at all. Example: a link that drops and recovers during a lost round's dim resets the level to 1 and ends the dim early.
proposed: In `lampControls`: `hold(s, owner: "lost" | "breath" | "link", level: number | null, rate)`. `Lamp` carries `holds: Record<owner, number>`, and the effective target is `min(1, …holds)`. `setLevel` leaves the public `LampRig` and is replaced by `hold`.
effect: The two sentinel comparisons go. Each writer releases only its own hold.

title: CardView carries an interaction model that only the tutorial uses
problem: CardView is two modules in one. One paints a face or back with its a11y label. The other is a press and selection interaction: a spring lift of `-14` when `selected`, plus a press rise and tilt.
proposed: make CardView a pure painter (face/back + a11y). Move press and lift into a `TutorialCard` wrapper next to its only caller, or have the tutorial reuse the hand's lift via `handRowHeadroom`. Then `noLift` goes away.
effect: the interface narrows (`noLift`, `onPress`, `selected` leave the painter). The table stops paying for per-card animation state it never uses.

title: `flightPhysics.ts` is a grab bag whose name misleads, guarded by an import-ownership scan
problem: Low cohesion; the name misleads on half its contents. `flightHooks.test.ts` pins "each helper has one component owner" by regex over import lines, which is a substitute for module boundaries. Real duplication: `readThrownPlay` 588-594 and `readExchangeLegs` 630-633 carry the identical "own hand slot, else `HAND_SCALE/FIELD_SCALE` at the seat" expression.
proposed: `impact.ts`: tiers, trauma, flinch, shake, flare, `landWobble`. `tableLayout.ts`: anchors (F4). `passes.ts`: `comboKey`, `trickClosedWithWinner`, `passedSeats`, `seatsJustPassed`.
effect: `flightHooks.test.ts` is deleted. Each test file in `flightPhysics.test.ts` maps to one module.

title: Three hand-rolled countdowns; the seat ring and the turn chip show the same window from independent clocks
problem: The same concept ("a server window of N seconds, restarted by a key, optionally held") is implemented three ways. GameTable's comment (1086-1094) says the ring "sweeps over the same window the viewer's chip counts down". The two run on unrelated timers (interval ticks against an animation duration plus `Date.now` accumulation), and their hold semantics are implemented separately.
proposed: The ring drives its `withTiming` from `seconds*1000 - elapsedMs()`; the chip and the mark render `left`. Pure core: `countdownStep(state, now)`.
effect: About 60 lines are replaced by one tested hook. The chip and ring cannot drift by construction.

title: `CardItem` has 30 props, a boolean disguised as a number, and two "deal" mechanisms
problem: `dealDelay` is documented as "ms to wait, or -1", but its only caller passes `descending ? 0 : -1` (1355). It is a boolean, and `dealDelayRef`/`withDelay` always wait 0.
proposed: `pose` becomes `poseOf(entry, state, now)` with one call site feeding style, rect and the landing reaction.
effect: The props become about 12 grouped values, and the comparator shrinks (pairs with F8). The descend duration moves to `Motion` (`Motion.exchange.*`) instead of a component literal.

title: Notice float, opening gate and veils are state machines written as render-time `setState`
problem: The float reducer tracks four "last seen" values (`passSeen`, `errorSeen`, `autoSeen`, `withdrawnSeen`) inline. Its only tests are native mounts (`passMarker`, `onlineErrorFloat`, `offlineAutoPass`, `onlineAutoPass`). The veil decision is five booleans with long comments.
proposed: Pure `nextFloat(prev, input)` in `components/table/tableFloat.ts` and `tableVeils(input): Record<VeilRole, boolean>` plus a `VeilRegion` component in `tableVeils.ts`; the veil test then keys on `<VeilRegion>` instead of indentation.
effect: About 60 lines of render-phase logic become two tested pure functions. The whitespace-sensitive scan goes away.

title: GIOCA and PASSA each hand-roll the press scale, and the garnet gradient stops live twice
problem: The inventory duplicate is real: the same `setPress`/`pressVal`/cancel/`pressStyle` block appears twice. The gradient's stops belong to the gradient, yet each consumer restates them.
proposed: `usePressScale(enabled: boolean): { onPressIn; onPressOut; style }` in actions.tsx. `Gradient.garnet` becomes `{ colors, locations }` in `lib/tokens.ts`.
effect: about 20 lines go, and a third garnet surface cannot get the stops wrong.

title: `useCardRect` takes its mapper inputs from a private worklets field
problem: `__closure` is an internal of the worklets Babel plugin. If it is renamed or reshaped, the `?? {}` turns it into "no inputs".
proposed: `useCardRect(key, read, inputs: readonly SharedValue<unknown>[])`, with callers naming what `read` reads. Alternatively, a test that fails when `__closure` is absent on a worklet.
effect: the dependence on a library internal becomes explicit or guarded.

title: Notice timing puts a reading hold in `Motion` and ignores reduced motion for two shapes
problem: `chip` and `float` take `Motion.mark.{enter, hold, exit}` whatever `reduceMotion` is. `pill` goes through `motionMs("notice", reduceMotion)`. `hold: 1000` is a reading duration, which components/CLAUDE.md says belongs in `Reading`, not `Motion`.
proposed: `hold: Reading.mark`, and enter/exit via `motionMs("mark", reduceMotion)`.
effect: one rule for notice timing, and the token audit stops seeing a reading time in `Motion`.

title: Unused motion knob and component-literal durations
problem: A parameter with one value is a hypothetical seam. The two 500 ms literals are motion durations outside `Motion`, so they escape the reduced-motion and token checks.
proposed: drop the `durationMs` prop and use `SWEEP_MS`. Move both literals to `Motion.duration.*`.
effect: three fewer local knobs.

title: Rank letter-spacing is defined twice, and the joker rank ignores scale
problem: `LETTER_SPACING = -0.5` in cardFaceModel feeds `rankTextWidth`, which is the geometry that keeps index boxes from overlapping. CardView's stylesheet hardcodes `letterSpacing: -0.5` separately, so if one changes, the measured width no longer matches the painted width. `rankTextJoker` also pins `FontSize.xs` / `lineHeight: 12`, which overrides the scaled rank box.
proposed: import the constant into the style. Derive the joker size from the same scale.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Render churn from fresh defaults and per-frame state
problem: The `placementPoints = {}` (357) and `disconnectedSeats = {}` (371) defaults are new objects on every render for replay, capture and bench callers. `placementPoints` is in the deps of the round-over effect in useTableFeedback (355), so that effect reruns on every render. `readExchange` returns a new object while an exchange is active (flightPhysics.ts:425-440), and that object is in the `tableA11yLabel` memo deps (GameTable 779).
proposed: hoist the defaults to module-level constants, key the memo on exchange fields, keep `hasMore` as state that is set only when it changes, and compute `shakeOffset` once.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: BenchScreen run latch has no finally
problem: `benchRunning` and the drain interval are reset only on the success path. A throw outside the per-scenario catch (`benchScenarios()`, diag, `recorder.postTo`) leaves the latch set forever and the interval running, and unmount does no cleanup. This is dev-only.
proposed: run the body in a non-hook helper with try/finally, and add an unmount cleanup effect.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Platform branches scattered instead of behind one seam
problem: The web overflow-clip quirk (a focused child scrolls a `hidden` box) is written twice with two different casts: `GameTable.tsx:169-170` (`WEB_CLIP`, cast via `unknown as ViewStyle`) and `hand.tsx:1431` (`"clip" as "hidden"`). The "iOS cannot grey a view with a filter" quirk is split between `greyLayer.tsx:8-14` and `useLinkHold.ts:15-17, 76-80`, plus the `grey` prop doc at `feltCanvas.tsx:50`. `feltCanvas.tsx:57`'s `IOS` is a different quirk (opaque Skia).
proposed: `lib/platform.ts`: `export const clipOverflow: ViewStyle | null;` and `export const viewFilterGrey: boolean;`. `hapticsAvailable` exported from `lib/device/feedback.ts`. A `harnessData(state)` usable on Text and View.
effect: one place per quirk (about 8 sites); a new surface cannot get the cast wrong.

title: `useTableFeedback` recomputes the round and match outcome GameTable already has
problem: The 17-input interface exists to rebuild a value the caller holds. The sound and the visuals decide "outcome known" by different rules in two files. This is not shown to be a bug, but it is a locality problem.
proposed: `useTableFeedback({ ..., outcome: RoundOutcome, matchOutcome: RoundOutcome, scored: boolean })`, with `scored` decided once next to `roundOutcomeFor`.
effect: 7 inputs drop to 3; one rule for "decided".

title: Score pill and match-board derivation in GameTable
problem: pure geometry and labels sit in the component, beside the existing `components/table/scorePillModel.ts` and `lib/game/scorePill.ts`.
proposed: `pillAnchorFor(layout: TableLayout): PillAnchor` and `voteTop(anchor, open, scale)` in scorePillModel. `matchBoardFor(standings, players, winners, score, t)` in `lib/game/scorePill.ts`.
effect: about 45 lines become node-testable (`scorePillGeometry` and `scorePillStandings` already exist to extend).

title: `getComboLabel` is a pure label function living in a component, with a lossy key type
problem: `Record<string, TranslationKey>` loses exhaustiveness; an unknown type falls back to the raw `combo.type` string on screen.
proposed: move it to `components/table/spokenLabels.ts` (beside `lastPlayLabel`) as `Record<Combination["type"], TranslationKey>`.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.

title: Animation-lifetime boilerplate
problem: 55 `cancelAnimation(` calls across components (`useTableFeedback.ts` 10, `hand.tsx` 9, `seats.tsx` 7, `moments.tsx` 7, `pile.tsx` 6, …). 11 of them are the exact `useEffect(() => () => cancelAnimation(x), [x])` shape. `hand.tsx:388-399` cancels 7 values by hand.
proposed: `useOwnedValue<T>(init: T): SharedValue<T>`, a shared value cancelled on unmount.
effect: About 25 cleanup effects removed, and "forgot to cancel" becomes structural. `tests/ui-rules/infiniteAnimations.test.ts` can accept the owned hook as the cancellation.

title: Both particle adapters re-state the per-frame scene step, and the web one never idles
problem: The seam between the two is real (Skia Atlas vs 2D canvas). But the step order sits in both adapters and must stay in lockstep by hand: `emberFrame` `coneRainFrame` `step` `stepAir`, with its moth trace `layout` `layoutMotes` `mothPose` The native adapter skips idle frames (`:92-94`). The web adapter clears and redraws every rAF tick forever, including at rest with no lit motes.
proposed: One worklet in `particleSprites.ts`: `stepScene(scene: {s: Particles; air: Air; ember: EmberRun; rain: RainRun}, l: AirLight, dt: number, reduced: boolean, rng: Rng, out: Float32Array): {lit: number; moth: MothPose | null; mothSet: boolean; idle: boolean}`. Each adapter keeps only its draw. The web loop returns early on `idle` the way native does.
effect: About 10 duplicated lines become one call. Web stops redrawing an idle table.

title: "Where the chips end" is computed in two places; computeScreenPads is a pass-through
problem: `notificationTopOffset` (tableFrame.ts:201-216) rebuilds the chip bottom from raw inputs: `max(PAD_TOP*s, topPad) + surplus + CHIP_H + PAD_INNER*s`. That is the same value as GameTable's banner band top, `frame.tableTop + CHIP_H(scale) + frame.pad` (GameTable.tsx:1386; tableTop at tableFrame.ts:153, pad at 165). NotificationBanner (96-103) works out `surplusHeight/2` again instead of reading the frame.
proposed: export one `chipsBottom(frame, scale)` from tableFrame.ts. Make `notificationTopOffset` take a `TableFrame`. Delete `computeScreenPads`.
effect: one source of truth for the band under the chips. A change to chip padding can no longer move the table and leave the banner behind.

title: Settings rows are spelled out six times
problem: every row repeats `row`/`stackRow > rowLeft > RowIcon + label/sublabel + control`. The inventory duplicates (267-281=284-309, 236-248=252-264, 237-246=270-279, 267-276=317-326) are real. The haptics capability check is restated in settingsSheet.tsx:304 (ui-F14).
proposed: `SettingRow({ icon, label, sublabel, stacked, children })`.
effect: Not stated separately by the source.
